featured_reviews.name: Pratham Rajpurohit
featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience with Pratik Tutorials was honestly disappointing, especially as someone who joined in Class 11 and was not already academically strong.

First of all, I want to clarify that not all teachers were bad — the Biology teachers were genuinely supportive and respectful. But my experience with parts of the Physics and Chemistry faculty was very negative.

I struggled with Mathematics and had already moved away from it academically. Instead of helping students who were weak in certain concepts, some teachers would ask questions in front of the class in a way that felt more like public embarrassment than teaching. I remember being asked a basic division question in Chemistry class and when I answered incorrectly, instead of explaining, comments were made that made me feel unintelligent and ashamed in front of everyone. Students laughed and the situation became worse.

What hurt the most was not getting support when I clearly didn’t understand something. Being weak in one subject should not become a reason for humiliation. Over time, the jokes and comments made me feel isolated and embarrassed to speak or ask questions.

After that incident people kept making comments about my studies and whether I should continue. At one point, another student made a very insensitive remark suggesting I should “give up” instead of trying. Even if it was meant as a joke, comments like that can affect people deeply and should never be normalized in an educational environment.

I eventually started feeling mentally exhausted and emotionally low because I constantly felt judged for things I genuinely struggled with. Instead of gaining confidence, I started losing confidence socially and academically. I became quieter, avoided interacting, and started overthinking simple situations because I felt people would make fun of me again.

When I tried to speak about my concerns, I was told things were “just jokes,” but repeated humiliation does not feel like a joke when you are the student experiencing it.

Because I joined later than others, I also struggled socially. I often felt excluded from groups and activities and found it difficult to fit in.

Another thing I personally noticed was that a lot of focus seemed to go toward showcasing top-performing students and results. I understand institutions celebrate achievements, but from my perspective, success should not only mean highlighting students who were already performing strongly. Real support is helping average or struggling students improve as well.

The coaching often promoted itself as highly supportive and result-oriented, but in my experience, improvement still depended mostly on personal effort. Students who are already disciplined and strong may continue performing well, but students who need extra guidance, patience, and confidence-building may not always receive that level of support.

Academically too, I did not get the “basic to advanced” support that was promised. Doubts were not always cleared properly and students who were slower or less confident could easily feel left behind.

I also want parents to understand that once a student joins and a large fee is paid, many students may hesitate to speak openly about a negative experience. Some continue attending even when they feel uncomfortable because they don’t want to disappoint their parents or create problems.

I’m writing this because reviews don’t always show every side of an institution. Some students thrive in competitive environments, but others — especially introverted students or students who need patience, respect, and encouragement — may have a very different experience.

Please talk openly with your child after joining any coaching class. Every student learns differently, and support matters as much as teaching.

This review is based only on my personal experience

featured_reviews.name: Pratham Rajpurohit
featured_reviews.review_text:
Reply
Thank you for replying. I appreciate that you responded, but I want to clarify that my review was never about being unable to answer one question.

The issue was not that students laughed or that I got something wrong. Every student struggles at some point, especially someone joining six months later and trying to adjust.

I also want to clarify that the question I remember was not simply “6 ÷ 2” as described in the reply. My difficulty was understanding in that moment — and even if a student cannot answer a basic question, that should become a teaching moment, not a moment of humiliation.

What affected me was what happened afterward.

After I could not answer, comments and jokes started instead of explanation. The teacher later asked the same question to another student sitting in front of me, and that student also could not answer. I quietly said something like, “I had dropped Maths, but you still have Maths, so why couldn’t you answer?” The teacher heard that and the situation turned into more public jokes.

Comments were made like questioning why I chose Science, suggesting I should have stayed in another stream, and using mocking language instead of helping me understand. There were also comments outside the classroom that felt unnecessary and unprofessional, including lines meant to sound funny such as “system hil gaya kya” and “Elvish bhai ko bulaun kya" which was said by well known, educated teacher. Those moments felt less like teaching and more like entertainment at one student’s expense.

Students then continued making jokes among themselves and one student even made a comment suggesting I should “take dropout from life.” Whether intended as humor or not, comments like that can affect someone deeply and create an unhealthy environment.

I want to be clear: I am not saying teachers cannot ask questions or that students should never be corrected. I am saying there is a difference between correcting a student and making them feel embarrassed for not knowing something.

I also never claimed all teachers were bad. My review was about how this specific experience affected me personally.

If a student cannot answer, the response should be explanation and support — not taunts, labels, or trying to look cool by making jokes in front of the class.

This review remains my personal experience and I am sharing it because I do not want other students who are academically weaker, quieter, or joining late to feel the same way
